sentences.text:
Dhannu @ Dhanua vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 19
January, 2023

Author: Anjuli Palo
Bench: Anjuli Palo
In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh At Jabalpur Cra No. 8834 of 2022 (Dhannu
@ Dhanua Vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh) Dated : 19-01-2023 Shri Paritosh Trivedi -
Advocate for the appellant.
Ms. Pushpanjali Dwivedi - Panel Lawyer for the State.
Heard on admission.

entities.text: High Court Of Madhya Pradesh At Jabalpur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Heard on I.A.No.18556/2022, which is first application filed on behalf of the appellants for
suspension of sentence and grant of bail.
The appellant has been convicted by the trial Court under Sections 450, 376(2)(n) of Ipc and
sentenced to R.I. for 2 years with fine of Rs.1000/- and R.I. for 10 years with fine of Rs. 2000/-
respectively with default stipulation.

Learned counsel for the appellant has submitted that the trial Court has not properly appreciated the oral and documentary evidence available on record and committed error in convicting the appellant for aforesaid offences.

The trial Court has failed to appreciate that it is a case of consent,
which reflects from the statement of the prosecutrix itself.

The appellant is in custody and there is a bleak possibility of disposal of this appeal in near future, therefore, the custodial sentence of the appellant may be suspended and he may be released on bail.
Learned Panel Lawyer has opposed the prayer for bail.
I have heard learned counsel for the parties.
From the perusal of statement of the prosecutrix, it appears that the prosecutrix was major at the time of incident and at that time she was not willing to marry the appellant.

Looking to the examination-in-chief and para 20 of the cross-examination of the prosecutrix, I find it to be a fit case to suspend the jail sentence of the appellant and to release him on bail, therefore,
without commenting on the merit of the case, the application is allowed.

I t is directed that subject to depositing the fine amount, if not already deposited and on furnishing a personal bond in a sum of Rs.40,000/- (Rupees Forty Thousand only) with one surety each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court concerned, the custodial sentence of appellant Dhannu @ Dhanua shall remain suspended and he shall be released on bail for securing his Dhannu @ Dhanua vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 19 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199900065/
1 presence before the trial Court on 6.7.2023 and on such other dates as may be fixed in this regard during pendency of this appeal.
